Binary Search Trees

let the structure do the halving

A Guessing Game

I'm thinking of a number from 1 to 128.
You get seven guesses.
After each one I say lower, higher, or you win.

Talk to your neighbor · TTYN
What should your first guess be?
  • A. 1
  • B. 32
  • C. 64
  • D. Any number: it is luck
✓ Answer
C. 64: whatever the answer, half of the numbers are gone.

Binary Search

Talk to your neighbor · TTYN
Binary search on a vector of n numbers. What has to be true of the numbers?
  • A. They are sorted
  • B. n is a power of 2
  • C. No two are equal
  • D. They are ints
✓ Answer
A. And the middle has to be one step away: v[mid] is O(1).

From a List to a Tree

Tree Terms

The BST Property

For every node, not just the root. No value appears twice.

Talk to your neighbor · TTYN
Which insertion order builds this BST?
  • A. 50, 70, 55, 57, 40, 30
  • B. 30, 40, 50, 55, 57, 70
  • C. 50, 70, 40, 30, 55, 57
  • D. 50, 30, 40, 70, 55, 57
✓ Answer
D. A and C put 30 under 40; B makes a chain.
Talk to your neighbor · TTYN
How many of these are BSTs?
  • A. 1
  • B. 2
  • C. 3
  • D. 4
✓ Answer
B. 2: A and C. In B, 9 is left of 8; in D, 10 is.

Implementing a BST


template <class Item>
class BST {
public:
    BST();
    ~BST();
    bool isEmpty() const;
    unsigned getSize() const;
    void insert(const Item& it);
    bool contains(const Item& it) const;
    // ...
private:
    class Node;
    Node* myRoot;
    unsigned myNumItems;
};
      

class Node {
public:
    Item  myItem;
    Node* myLeft;   // smaller
    Node* myRight;  // bigger

    Node(const Item& it);
    void insert(const Item& it);
    bool contains(const Item& it) const;
    // ...
};

Inserting

Talk to your neighbor · TTYN
Where does insert put every new node? 

template <class Item>
BST<Item>::Node::Node(const Item& it) {
    myItem  = it;
    myLeft  = nullptr;
    myRight = nullptr;
}
  • A. At the root
  • B. As a leaf
  • C. In the middle level
  • D. Wherever there is room
✓ Answer
B. It walks down until a child is missing, and the new node has no children of its own.

Searching, Shape and Removal

the same keys, a different order, a different tree

Tree Shape

Searching

Talk to your neighbor · TTYN
Seven nodes on the left, six on the right. As n grows, what does contains cost in each?
  • A. O(lg n) and O(lg n)
  • B. O(lg n) and O(n)
  • C. O(n) and O(n)
  • D. O(1) and O(n)
✓ Answer
B. The cost is the height. A bushy tree is lg n tall; a list is n.

Postorder

Talk to your neighbor · TTYN
The destructor has to delete every node. In which order is that safe?
  • A. Preorder
  • B. Inorder
  • C. Postorder
  • D. Any order
✓ Answer
C. Delete a node only after its children. Deleting 57 first loses the way to 36 and 84.

Expression Trees

Talk to your neighbor · TTYN
Height: the nodes on the longest path down from the root. A full tree of height 3 has 7 nodes. Height 4?
  • A. 8
  • B. 12
  • C. 15
  • D. 16
✓ Answer
C. 15: each level doubles.
height1234h
nodes137152h − 1
So n nodes fit in about lg n levels, if the tree is full.

Computing Height

Talk to your neighbor · TTYN
Computing the height of a whole BST of n nodes. What does it cost?
  • A. O(1)
  • B. O(lg n)
  • C. O(n)
  • D. O(n²)
✓ Answer
C. Every node is asked once, like a postorder traversal.

Removing a Leaf

Talk to your neighbor · TTYN
remove(57): 57 has two children. Which value can move into its node and keep this a BST?
  • A. 36
  • B. 42
  • C. 84
  • D. 99
✓ Answer
B. 42, the largest on the left: still bigger than all of the left, smaller than all of the right. 63 would work too.

The STL set and map

the library's BST, finished and balanced

The STL set

Using a set

calldoescost
s.insert(x)adds x, unless it is thereO(lg n)
s.erase(x)removes xO(lg n)
s.count(x)1 if x is there, 0 if notO(lg n)
s.find(x)an iterator to x, or s.end()O(lg n)
s.size(), s.empty()how many; are there noneO(1)
s.begin(), s.end()the smallest item; one past the largestO(1)
s.clear()removes everythingO(n)

#include <set>. Sorted, each item once, usually a red-black tree (a balanced BST). All of it: cppreference.com: std::set

Talk to your neighbor · TTYN
A set holds 1,000,000 words. About how many words does count(w) compare w with?
  • A. 1,000,000
  • B. 500,000
  • C. 20
  • D. 1
✓ Answer
C. The tree stays balanced, so its height is about lg 1,000,000, about 20.

The STL map

Talk to your neighbor · TTYN
Each element of a map is a pair. Which line prints every key and its value? 

for (map<string, int>::iterator it = stock.begin();
     it != stock.end(); ++it) {
    // ?
}
  • A. cout << it << endl;
  • B. cout << it.first << ' ' << it.second << endl;
  • C. cout << it(first) << ' ' << it(second) << endl;
  • D. cout << it->first << ' ' << it->second << endl;
✓ Answer
D. it acts like a pointer to a pair: ->, as with a pointer to a Node.

Using a map

calldoescost
m[k]the value for k; adds k with 0 if it is missingO(lg n)
m.at(k)the value for k; throws if it is missingO(lg n)
m.count(k)1 if k is a key, 0 if notO(lg n)
m.find(k)an iterator to k's pair, or m.end()O(lg n)
m.erase(k)removes k and its valueO(lg n)
m.size(), m.empty()how many pairs; are there noneO(1)
it->first, it->secondthe key and the value an iterator points toO(1)

#include <map>. Pairs with unique keys, sorted by key, usually a red-black tree. Iterators go in ascending order of keys. All of it: cppreference.com: std::map

Counting Words

Cost

set, mapyour BST
insert, find, eraseO(lg n), alwaysO(lg n) bushy, O(n) a list

The difference is balance: the library's tree rebalances as it grows, with rotations like Monday's.

Choosing a Container

You need toUse
reach item i, mostly add at the endvector
add and remove at the front, never indexlist
take the newest firststack

look a value up by its keymap

Week 11 Recap

  • Smaller items go left, bigger right, for every node
  • insert and contains are the guessing game: compare, then go one way
  • New nodes always arrive as leaves
  • The cost is the height: lg n when bushy, n when a list
  • Inorder comes out sorted; the destructor is postorder
  • Removing a node with children: copy in the largest on its left
  • set and map are balanced BSTs: O(lg n), always
